subject: general
question: Two circles of radii 10 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. What is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
solution:
Given:

PA = 10 cm

QA = 12 cm

AB = 16 cm

Concept used:

Pythagoras Theorem 

Distance between two centres divides the common chord in halves and is perpendicular to the common chord as well.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61f357c9d16f589ee819a824fd43d4f5f7b87e77858f3f33c7f2df5498ec2072.png] 

AR = RB = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

AB is perpendicular to PQ. 

Hence, PQ divides AB in halves.

Now,

PR = sqrt {10² - 8²} = 6 cm

QR = sqrt {12² - 8² } = 4√5 cm

Thus, PQ = (6 + 4√5) cm

**∴ The distance between their centres is (6 + 4√5) cm.**
